# “The Software Era Is Over for Insurance Agencies”: SUPERAGENT AI Launches 3.0, an AI Business Partner That Does the Work Itself  
PR Newswire  
SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 11, 2026  
*Launching today, SUPERAGENT 3.0 gives every insurance agency what its founders call the first glimpse of what Vertical AGI may look like in a single industry. Owners talk and watch a campaign get built, a book of calls get scored, or a producer gets trained. Nothing touches an agency’s book without the owner’s approval.*  
SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Ask a generic AI chatbot to find your 90-day renewals and you get a paragraph. Starting today, insurance agency owners can ask their agency the same question and get the list, then the campaign to work it, then a card requesting permission to launch. That difference is the product SUPERAGENT AI, Inc. released to the public this morning: SUPERAGENT AI 3.0, the AI Business Partner for insurance agencies.  
The company is framing the release as a generational break with how agencies have run for decades. Instead of a stack of software an owner operates, 3.0 is a partner an owner talks to. It reads the agency’s live data, knows insurance the way a veteran producer knows their book, and executes the work itself: campaigns, call analysis, producer training, record updates. Every action that would change the agency’s book waits behind an approval card for the owner’s click.
“The software era is over for insurance agencies. The partner era starts today,” said Vlada Lotkina, CEO of SUPERAGENT AI. “For twenty years this industry has paid an invisible tax: owners and producers spending their days operating tools instead of selling. With 3.0 you don’t operate anything. You say what you need, out loud or in a sentence, and it gets done in front of you, with your permission on every change. It is the business partner every owner wishes they’d had on day one.”  
**Four tools and five steps, replaced by one sentence**  
Until now, “using AI” in an Insurance Agency meant exporting a report, downloading a spreadsheet, pasting it into a chatbot, asking a question, and then returning to the software to act on the answer. Four tools and five steps for one outcome. SUPERAGENT 3.0 collapses that entire loop into one conversation, on live agency data, inside the platform where the work actually happens.  
What that looks like in practice on day one:  
- A failing campaign is diagnosed, its bottleneck named, and its capacity doubled, in a single chat thread.
- “Build me a winback campaign for every lead we lost this quarter” produces a complete, ready-to-activate campaign: playbook, steps, timing, inbox, AI agents assigned to the call steps.
- Every customer call is scored 0 to 100 across an eight-dimension quality framework, and the agency’s costliest objection can be pulled straight from its own conversations.
**About SUPERAGENT AI**  
SUPERAGENT AI is the AI workforce platform purpose-built for insurance agencies. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco, SUPERAGENT unifies inbound and outbound calling, campaigns, quoting data capture, call intelligence, and producer training into a single platform trusted by more than 500 insurance agencies across the United States. With SUPERAGENT 3.0, the platform becomes the AI Business Partner for insurance agencies: talk to it, and it does the work. Learn more at [www.getsuperagent.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4749753-1&h=581258128&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.getsuperagent.com%2F&a=www.getsuperagent.com).

results.name: Changelog - Product Updates | Superagent
results.content:
August 15, 2026
## Context Guardrails for everything agents consume  
Score web pages, email, files, agent skills, and public GitHub MCP repositories before an agent trusts them.  
Runtime Guardrails decide what an agent may do. Context Guardrails decide what an agent may consume.  
Agents fetch pages, open files, install skills, and connect MCP servers without reviewing any of it. Superagent now scores that untrusted context first, so agents keep full capability without inheriting hostile input.
### Five origins, available now  
- **Web pages**— domain identity, redirect chains, hidden DOM, and rendered page text. New lookups return a preliminary identity score immediately and finish the deep scan in the background.
- **Email**— sender authentication, phishing and injection patterns, attachments, and outbound links.
- **Files**— public text and PDFs, with type consistency, encoded instructions, and prompt injection checks. File bytes are never stored.
- **Agent skills**— GitHub publisher identity, requested capabilities, hidden instructions, and install hooks. Skill files are treated as untrusted data and are never executed.
- **MCP repositories**— static review of public GitHub MCP servers, including tool descriptions, schemas, instructions, hooks, and secrets. Superagent never connects to a live MCP endpoint or runs the server.  
Full repositories remain covered by [repository red teaming](https://www.superagent.sh/docs/red-team/repository-reports). Packages remain covered by [supply-chain scanning](https://www.superagent.sh/docs/pr-scans/supply-chain-scanning).

results.title: Changelog - Product Updates | Superagent
results.snippet: August 15, 2026 ## Context Guardrails for everything agents consume Score web pages, email, files, agent skills, and public GitHub MCP repositories before an agent trusts them. Runtime Guardrails decide what an agent may do. Context Guardrails decide what an agent may consume. Agents fetch pages, open files, install skills, and connect MCP servers without reviewing any of it. Superagent now scores that untrusted context first, so agents keep full capability without inheriting hostile input. ### Five origins, available now - **Web pages**— domain identity, redirect chains, hidden DOM, and rendered page text. New lookups return a preliminary identity score immediately and finish the deep scan in the background. - **Email**— sender authentication, phishing and injection patterns, attachments, and outbound links. - **Files**— public text and PDFs, with type consistency, encoded instructions, and prompt injection checks. File bytes are never stored. - **Agent skills**— GitHub publisher identity, requested capabilities, hidden instructions, and install hooks. Skill files are treated as untrusted data and are never executed. - **MCP repositories**— static review of public GitHub MCP serve
